scenes.say: MTBF and MTTR. Two numbers every maintenance team hears about. Here's what they mean.
scenes.html:
Explainer
MTBF & MTTR
What they mean, in one minute
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: MTBF is mean time between failures: total running time, divided by the number of failures.
scenes.html:
MTBF · Mean Time Between Failures
Running time ÷
number of failures
Higher is better
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: MTTR is mean time to repair: total repair time, divided by the number of repairs.
scenes.html:
MTTR · Mean Time To Repair
Repair time ÷
number of repairs
Lower is better
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Example. A machine runs six hundred hours and fails four times. Six hundred divided by four is an MTBF of one hundred fifty hours.
scenes.html:
Example: MTBF
600 h ÷ 4 failures
150 h
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: The four repairs took six hours in total. Six divided by four is an MTTR of one and a half hours.
scenes.html:
Example: MTTR
6 h ÷ 4 repairs
1.5 h
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Put them together and you get availability: MTBF divided by MTBF plus MTTR. Here that's about ninety-nine percent.
scenes.html:
Availability
MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR)
≈ 99%
150 ÷ 151.5 = 0.990
Standard reliability definitions
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: To improve MTBF, fix root causes, and keep up with lubrication and preventive maintenance, so failures happen less often.
scenes.html:
Raise MTBF
Fix root causes.
Keep up the PMs.
Fail less often
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: To improve MTTR, have the parts, the drawings and the know-how ready, so each repair is faster. Repair time includes finding the fault and waiting for parts.
scenes.html:
Lower MTTR
Parts. Drawings.
Know-how.
Repair time includes diagnosis and waiting for parts
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: One tip: count failures the same way every time, or the numbers won't compare from month to month.
scenes.html:
Tip
Count failures
the same way, every time
Syon Automation LLC
